title: Everyone Carries an Older Story
core_idea: Held as a belief rather than fact, the idea of rebirth can soften how we see others by reminding us that everyone carries an unseen history.
text: Imagine, for a moment, that the stranger beside you on the train has lived many lives before this one. In traditions that hold a belief in rebirth, this idea is not only about the past. It can also change how we see each other now. If every person carries a long, unseen story, then the impatient driver, the quiet colleague, the friend who reacts too strongly, may be carrying more than we know. Whether or not rebirth is real, the thought itself can soften us. It reminds us that no one arrives in this moment empty-handed. Each of us is still learning. Each of us deserves a little patience on the way.
description: A reflection on how the idea of past lives, held gently as belief, can invite more patience with one another.
